label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 159.

diagnosis.hypothesis: A poison message is stuck at the head of the ledger. Provider event evt_000260 (provider-events partition 1, offset 115) arrived at about 16:27:03. It carries an amount that is not a positive integer in cents. ledger-consumer had been redeployed at 16:27:01 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. With that setting it retries the same message forever, with backoff capped at 15 s, and never commits past it. The ledger group's lag therefore grows on all partitions, so the money check cannot settle to its cutoff. That is the BooksBehindProvider alert. payment-confirmer reads the same message but runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it dead-lettered the event once and moved on with zero lag. The data leaves some points open. I did not see the event's actual amount, or why the provider sent it. I did not see what BAD_EVENTS the ledger ran before 16:27:01. Lag rising on partitions 0 and 2 as well suggests the retry blocks the whole consumer, not only partition 1.

evidence.shows: The ledger keeps posting some events, while payment-confirmer dead-lettered one event around 16:28.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 16:27:01 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. Everything else was deployed at 16:25:34.
Starting 16:27, ledger retries climb to 9 and ledger lag grows to 72 on each of partitions 0, 1 and 2. Confirmer lag stays 0 with no retries.
ledger-consumer repeatedly logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/1＠115, with error 'amount must be positive integer cents', attempts 3 to 9, at a 15 s backoff.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message, provider-events/1＠115, for the same amount error.

The trace shows the message is evt_000260, which webhook-receiver accepted and queued at offset 115. The confirmer dead-lettered it on its first attempt. The ledger fails it again and again with outcome will_retry.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before the 16:27:01 deploy, which presumably handled bad events by dead-lettering them, so it skips offset 1/115 and drains its lag. After that, inspect evt_000260 in the dead-letter store. Then check with the provider whether the charge or refund is real, and book it by hand or repair it if needed. Finally, run money_check to confirm the lag has cleared and the books match.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, so lag rises briefly. If the earlier settings dead-letter bad events, evt_000260 will not be booked in the ledger, and money_check may report it as missing until someone handles it by hand. If the earlier settings also retried bad events, the rollback does not unblock the consumer. Nothing already booked is changed.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). Booking is idempotent, so replaying events is safe.
